items.title: Haskell http-core plus Haskell scaffold and resolver integrity
items.notes: Current slice. Locally validated with GHC 9.4.8, 19 Hspec examples, 96% expression coverage, and 95% alternative coverage.

items.title: Language-neutral build-tool contract and shared fixture schema
items.notes: PR #9151 defines the reconciled v1 conformance contract, strict fixture schema, representative Windows override case, CI schema tests, and security boundary. It unlocks every existing build-tool remediation lane, missing Java/Kotlin/Dart implementations, and the future OCaml build tool.

items.title: Cross-implementation build-tool fixture runner and inventory gate
items.notes: Selected after PR #9151 merged because one safe non-execution runner, adapter manifest, domain result schemas, and representative corpus unlock the Go oracle, every existing front-door remediation, Java/Kotlin/Dart implementations, and OCaml promotion.

items.title: Add the trusted execution sandbox and adversarial execution corpus
items.notes: Newly separated after the contract security review. Require fail-closed filesystem and network isolation, no-follow materialization/output, direct argv, sanitized environments, and process-tree wall/CPU/memory/output/workspace/process-count limits before any execution fixture can run.

items.title: Bring the Go build tool to the canonical contract
items.notes: Wire structured Starlark context/commands and complete the B05 Windows executor contract.

items.title: Remediate all 12 existing build-tool front doors against shared fixtures
items.notes: Deliver one independent engine per PR; explicitly review the shared C#/F# engine exception.

items.title: Add language-native Java and Kotlin build tools
items.notes: Use shared JVM fixture infrastructure but separate idiomatic engines.

items.title: Add the Dart build tool
items.notes: Must pass the same plan, resolver, execution, and platform fixtures as the reference.

items.title: Define OCaml emerging-lane and denominator-safe reporter contracts
items.notes: OCaml remains outside the established denominator until all promotion gates pass.

items.title: Add OCaml scaffolding, build integration, CI, capabilities, and logic-gates
items.notes: Use OCaml 5.2.1, opam 2.5.x, Dune 3.17.2 (the nearest available compatible release; 3.16.1 is absent from opam), Alcotest, bisect_ppx, and ocamlformat.

items.title: Port graph, directed-graph, and state-machine to OCaml
items.notes: This dependency chain validates opam metadata, resolver edges, BUILD order, and affected-node expansion.

items.title: Implement the OCaml build tool and review 16-lane promotion
items.notes: Require conformance, two-way Go plan interchange, three-OS CI, capability enforcement, and explicit backlog acceptance.

items.title: Close the 13-package Dart-only 14-of-15 frontier
items.notes: Deliver small dependency-shaped PRs: ML, trig/wave, data structures, ciphers, document-ast, and uuid.

items.title: Port http1 to Haskell on the new http-core
items.notes: Next protocol dependency node; validate the repaired Cabal dependency graph.

items.title: Close Haskell event-loop and brotli
items.notes: Keep the event loop generic and portable; use byte-exact Brotli conformance vectors.

items.title: Close paired Java/Kotlin high-consensus families
items.notes: Start with lz78/deflate, zstd, and state-machine, then move through shared dependency chains.

items.title: Close Swift/Dart data-structure, storage, parser, WASM, ML, and protocol families
items.notes: Use generated grammars and dependency-first storage/compiler sequences.

items.title: Expand through 9-language and then 5-8-language portable packages
items.notes: Recompute and reprioritize after every merged wave.

items.title: Classify all singleton families and enforce declared parity work
items.notes: Current singleton leaders are Rust 538, Python 86, and TypeScript 84; do not port blindly.

items.title: Review C/C++ graduation and native build-tool requirements
items.notes: Keep both emerging until package/scaffold/build-tool maturity and applicability are explicit.
